text:
maria: Heads-up — our Windows CI started failing on python 3.11 and 3.10 with the SDK when company root CA is used. Error is ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: certificate verify failed.

alex: repro steps? Windows native or WSL?

maria: native Windows runner (hosted agent). Quick repro:
```python
import redwood
client = redwood.Client()
client.generate("hello")
```
stack: SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED (ssl.SSLCertVerificationError)

sam: do you have REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or SSL_CERT_FILE set in the env? requests/urllib3 respect those.

maria: no env vars. We rely on company-managed root certs installed in Windows cert store. Historically requests used certifi, but we thought Windows cert store would be consulted by OpenSSL on Windows builds.

alex: this is tricky — python's ssl on Windows doesn't automatically use the Windows cert store unless you use certifi or a custom SSLContext. On 3.8-3.9 we saw different builds behave differently. Which redwood-sdk version?

maria: redwood-sdk==0.14.2 (transitive: urllib3 2.x, requests 2.31).

jordan: I hit something similar months ago. Workaround was to point to the enterprise CA bundle file and set SSL_CERT_FILE or pass cafile to ssl.SSLContext.load_verify_locations. Example: export SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/to/enterprise.pem

maria: workaround works but it's awkward for Windows and onboarding docs don't mention it. New hires hit this on first sample app.

sam: is this happening for both sync and async clients? Our async path uses httpx by default (async) which has its own TLS stack.

maria: only tested sync so far. Will try async shortly.

alex: another piece — on Windows + python 3.11, OpenSSL build options matter. If the interpreter was compiled without Windows cert store integration you must provide cafile. Could be a CI image change.

maria: confirmed: async client (redwood.AsyncClient) also fails on 3.11 Windows.

jordan: two things to track: (1) improve SDK UX so people don't have to know about cert vars on Windows, (2) document a clear onboarding note for Windows runners. Also typing/async ergonomics: the AsyncClient stubs don't show context manager support in our types, folks get linter errors.

alex: feature request: add client constructor option `ca_bundle` that accepts a path or bytes and ensures we call `ssl_context.load_verify_locations(cafile=...)` for both sync and async transports. Also add `prefer_windows_certs` flag that tries to load certs from Windows store when available.

sam: +1 for `ca_bundle`. Also request to expose `retry_on_tls_error` config — currently SDK retries on network errors and we observe repeated TLS failures causing long retry storms in onboarding flows. Make TLS verification errors non-retryable by default.

maria: example log extract:
```
requests.exceptions.SSLError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.redwood.com', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /v1/generate (Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError(\"[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:997)\")))
```

alex: can we detect corporate CA automatically? Not reliably across Windows images. But we can add smarter defaults: check env vars, check common paths, allow `certifi.where()` override. Also publish a small helper `redwood.util.get_ca_bundle()` that returns a path to use.

jordan: typing fix: AsyncClient lacks `__aenter__/__aexit__` annotations for proper `async with` use in stubs. File: `stubs/async_client.pyi` needs updates. Also add `ca_bundle` parameter to `__init__` signature in both .pyi and runtime.

maria: low-friction doc change request: add a section "Windows CI: cert bundle and env vars" to quickstart. New hires hit this 3 times this week.

ci-bot: Created PR #1234 -- "py: add ca_bundle option + windows cert docs" and queued windows CI run.

alex: will review PR. If tests show consistent fix we should backport to 0.14.x patch. Also open question: what minimum python versions to support? current matrix is 3.8-3.12. We should ensure our TLS tests run across them on Windows images.

sam: can someone add a small test that runs on windows-latest image and simulates loading a custom cafile? I can help author it.

maria: thanks — assigning to @alex and @sam to shepherd the fix and docs. I kept logs and minimal repro in the PR description.

alex: noted. I'll add the typing updates and change retry policy for TLS errors.

jordan: and I'll write the quickstart doc blurb + troubleshooting FAQ entry.

maria: huge thanks. This should reduce onboarding friction for Windows users. :raised_hands:
